name: Goi nhong ong
summary: Gỏi nhộng ong is a salad of young bee pupae from the U Minh honey harvest. The version to look for mixes the pupae with banana blossom.
origin: U Minh Hạ. The pupae were long a forest dish and now appear on visitor meals.
culture: When the honey is taken, the keeper cuts away a little young comb, called dọn tàn, so the colony can go on. That comb is the start of the dish.
howToEat: The young comb is boiled so the wax melts and the pupae rise. They are skimmed out and drained before cooking.
The same pupae are also batter-fried or made into mắm ong. Nhộng ong trộn bắp chuối, with banana blossom, is the plate singled out.
where: U Minh Hạ, on a forest day.
seoTitle: Goi nhong ong — U Minh bee-pupa salad
seoDescription: Gỏi nhộng ong is young bee pupae from the U Minh honey harvest, best known mixed with banana blossom.
